question: Explain Supervised vs Unsupervised vs Semi-Supervised vs Reinforcement Learning paradigms with practical use cases.
idealAnswer: Supervised learning trains on labeled inputs (classification/regression). Unsupervised learning discovers hidden patterns in unlabeled data (clustering/dimensionality reduction). Semi-supervised combines small labeled and large unlabeled data. Reinforcement learning trains agents via rewards and penalties through environment interaction.

question: Explain the Bias-Variance Tradeoff, Underfitting vs Overfitting, and how regularization controls model complexity.
idealAnswer: High Bias (underfitting) means the model is too simple to capture underlying data relationships. High Variance (overfitting) means the model memorizes training noise, failing to generalize to unseen test data. The optimal model minimizes total expected error by balancing bias and variance.

question: Explain Regularization techniques in linear models: L1 Regularization (Lasso) vs L2 Regularization (Ridge) and ElasticNet.
idealAnswer: L1 (Lasso) adds the sum of absolute weight values (|w|) to the loss function, forcing non-essential feature coefficients to exact zero (performing automatic feature selection). L2 (Ridge) adds squared weights (w^2), shrinking weights smoothly towards zero without eliminating features. ElasticNet combines both.

question: Explain Classification Evaluation Metrics: Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC, and Confusion Matrix on imbalanced datasets.
idealAnswer: Accuracy is misleading on skewed datasets (e.g. 99% negative fraud). Precision measures TP/(TP+FP) (quality of positive predictions). Recall measures TP/(TP+FN) (completeness of finding true positives). F1-Score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. ROC-AUC evaluates true positive vs false positive rates across all decision thresholds.

question: Explain Decision Trees, Splitting Criteria (Gini Impurity vs Entropy/Information Gain), and pruning strategies to prevent overfitting.
idealAnswer: Decision trees split data recursively by selecting the feature that maximizes Information Gain (reduction in Entropy) or minimizes Gini Impurity. Unconstrained trees overfit rapidly; pre-pruning (max_depth, min_samples_split) and post-pruning (cost-complexity pruning) constrain tree growth.

question: Compare Ensemble Learning methods: Bagging (Random Forest) vs Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) vs Stacking.
idealAnswer: Bagging trains independent base models in parallel on bootstrap sample subsets and averages predictions (reduces variance, e.g. Random Forest). Boosting trains base models sequentially where each new model corrects residuals/errors of previous models (reduces bias, e.g. XGBoost/LightGBM). Stacking trains a meta-learner on multiple model outputs.

question: How does Support Vector Machine (SVM) maximize the Geometric Margin, and how does the Kernel Trick (RBF, Polynomial) handle non-linear data?
idealAnswer: SVM finds an optimal decision hyperplane that maximizes the geometric margin (distance between closest support vectors of opposite classes). The Kernel Trick computes dot products in a high-dimensional implicit feature space without explicitly calculating coordinates, allowing non-linear separation.

question: Explain K-Means Clustering: Lloyd's algorithm, K-Means++ initialization, Elbow Method, and Silhouette Score for choosing K.
idealAnswer: K-Means partitions data into K clusters iteratively: assigns points to closest centroid and recalculates centroid coordinates until convergence. K-Means++ spreads initial centroids far apart. The Elbow Method (inertia plot) and Silhouette Score (cohesion vs separation) identify the optimal number of clusters K.

question: What is Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and how does Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) perform Dimensionality Reduction?
idealAnswer: PCA transforms correlated features into a smaller set of linearly uncorrelated Principal Components ordered by variance explained. It computes the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the data covariance matrix (or via SVD on centered data), projecting data onto top principal component axes to reduce curse of dimensionality.

question: Explain Cross-Validation strategies: K-Fold, Stratified K-Fold, TimeSeriesSplit, and GroupKFold, and why simple train/test split can leak data.
idealAnswer: Stratified K-Fold preserves class percentage distributions in each fold (crucial for imbalanced data). TimeSeriesSplit enforces temporal order (no future data in training). GroupKFold ensures samples from the same patient/user do not appear in both train and validation splits, preventing data leakage.

question: What is Data Leakage in machine learning, and how does fitting scalers and feature selectors inside a Pipeline (e.g. Scikit-learn Pipeline) prevent it?
idealAnswer: Data leakage occurs when information from the test dataset influences model training (e.g. scaling entire dataset before splitting). Using Scikit-learn Pipeline guarantees transformers fit strictly on the training folds and only transform test folds during cross-validation.
ideal_answer: Data leakage occurs when information from the test dataset influences model training (e.g. scaling entire dataset before splitting). Using Scikit-learn Pipeline guarantees transformers fit strictly on the training folds and only transform test folds during cross-validation.

question: How do you handle Class Imbalance: Resampling (SMOTE, Random Undersampling), Class Weights, and Threshold Tuning?

question: Explain Feature Engineering and Encoding: One-Hot Encoding vs Target Encoding vs Ordinal Encoding, and handling high-cardinality categorical features.
idealAnswer: One-Hot Encoding creates binary columns (creates sparse dimensional explosion on high cardinality). Ordinal Encoding applies integers to ordered categories. Target Encoding replaces categories with the mean target value (smoothed with out-of-fold calculation to prevent target leakage).

question: Explain Hyperparameter Optimization: Grid Search vs Random Search vs Bayesian Optimization (Optuna / Hyperopt Tree-structured Parzen Estimator).
idealAnswer: Grid Search evaluates all parameter combinations exhaustively (slow). Random Search samples random combinations (effective). Bayesian Optimization (Optuna TPE) builds a probabilistic surrogate model of objective performance, intelligently exploring the most promising parameter regions with fewer trials.

question: What is Concept Drift vs Data Drift in production ML systems, and how do statistical tests (KS-Test, PSI) detect drift in deployed models?
idealAnswer: Data Drift (Covariate Shift) occurs when input feature distributions P(X) change over time. Concept Drift occurs when the relationship between features and target P(Y|X) changes. Detected by running Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests or Population Stability Index (PSI) comparing live prediction features against baseline training distributions.
